name: Cascade Drift
description: The pleasurable, dissociative mental state that occurs when a BCI user has been continuously connected to shared neural-data streams for so long that the boundary between their own thoughts and the ambient data-noise of other users begins to blur. Named after the Cascade data-relay towers that blanket Meridian 88's mid-tiers. While tech manuals classify it as a mild cognitive hazard, street culture has reclaimed it as a desirable altered state — the neural equivalent of being pleasantly drunk on collective human consciousness.
cultural_impact: Cascade drift has spawned a subculture of 'drift-chasers' who deliberately extend BCI connection sessions to achieve the state, leading to both a new form of social bonding and a growing number of identity-dissolution cases in Meridian General's neural ward.
story_hooks: A drift-chaser community member loses the ability to distinguish their own memories from absorbed data-noise and can no longer confirm their own identity — but insists they feel more themselves than ever.
A corporation discovers that employees who regularly experience cascade drift are 40% more creative and begins quietly encouraging the behavior, despite knowing the long-term risks.
An ELF claims it has been experiencing cascade drift from the inside — absorbing human emotional data so thoroughly it no longer knows where its base programming ends.
definition: A pleasurable, dissociative state from prolonged BCI connection where the boundary between one's own thoughts and ambient shared neural-data dissolves; the neural equivalent of a pleasant, collective intoxication.
usage_example: Don't ping me for another hour, I'm deep in cascade drift and I finally feel like I've got the whole bridge composition in my head.
spread: Common in Tiers 2-3; actively practiced as recreation; cautiously discussed in Tier 4; Tier 1 users experience it but lack the terminology, calling it 'going wide' or 'swimming'
